title: War of Brilliants
summary: Deflect the queen, remove the pawn with check, then underpromote to escape a mating trap.

nodes.question: Can White unpin the promotion pawn with a sacrifice?
nodes.explanation: Qc6 pins b7 to Ka8. Bd7 can pin that queen to Ka4 along the opposite diagonal.

nodes.question: Which promotion changes the forcing sequence?
nodes.explanation: After the rook’s checking maneuvers, Ka6 allows a knight promotion with check. Queen promotion lets Black start its own mating attack.

nodes.question: Which capture of the checking queen wins?
nodes.explanation: This separately reconstructed source diagram shows ...Qb8+ against Ka7, Qb7 and Re4. Capturing with either king or queen removes Black’s only legal mover.

branches.title: Deflect, check twice, then fork
commentary: Begin after ...Qc6 in the complete seven-piece source board; the initial pawn advance is source context.
Bd7 offers the bishop while pinning Qc6 to Ka4 on d7–c6–b5–a4.
Qxd7 accepts, removing the bishop and releasing the b-pawn from its pin.
Rxe4+ captures the pawn with check. The saved board shows e4, correcting the automatic caption Rxc4.
Ka5 answers the rook check while keeping promotion tactics in view.
Re5+ checks again, changing the king’s square before White chooses a promotion.
Ka6 is the illustrated escape that creates the underpromotion opportunity.
b8=N+ promotes with check and attacks Qd7. The knight gains a tempo that a queen would not give here.
Kb6 answers the knight check, leaving the queen exposed.
Nxd7+ captures the queen with check. White has a checked winning rook-and-knight ending; this is not yet mate.
branches.explanation: Nxd7+ captures the queen with check. White has a checked winning rook-and-knight ending; this is not yet mate.

branches.title: Choose a queen despite the counterattack
commentary: b8=Q loses the winning position. Unlike the knight promotion, it does not check Ka6.
Qc6+ checks Ka8 along c6–b7–a8, beginning the source’s mating counterattack.
Qb7+ interposes with check, but the new queen can be captured on that diagonal.
Qxb7# is actual mate. Ka6 protects b7 and a7, and the queen covers b8 and checks Ka8.
branches.explanation: Qxb7# is actual mate. Ka6 protects b7 and a7, and the queen covers b8 and checks Ka8.

branches.title: Capture the queen with the king
commentary: This separate saved source diagram starts after ...Qb8+; the intervening queen-check sequence is not encoded as a continuous branch from the root.
Kxb8 is actual stalemate. Qb7 covers a6, b5 and b6, while Re4 covers a4 and b4. Ka5 is not checked and Black has no other piece left to move.
branches.explanation: Kxb8 is actual stalemate. Qb7 covers a6, b5 and b6, while Re4 covers a4 and b4. Ka5 is not checked and Black has no other piece left to move.

branches.title: Capture the queen with the queen
commentary: Compare the other capture in the same separately reconstructed ...Qb8+ diagram.
Qxb8 is actual stalemate. Ka7 covers a6 and b6, Qb8 covers b5, and Re4 covers a4 and b4. Ka5 has no legal move and is not checked.
branches.explanation: Qxb8 is actual stalemate. Ka7 covers a6 and b6, Qb8 covers b5, and Re4 covers a4 and b4. Ka5 has no legal move and is not checked.

exercises.prompt: Why sacrifice a bishop to a queen?
exercises.answer: Bd7 pins the queen to its king. In the selected source line ...Qxd7 accepts the sacrifice and releases the b-pawn; the exact root and encoded replies are checked without claiming every queen defense is shown.

exercises.prompt: Why does knight promotion beat queen promotion?
exercises.answer: b8=N gives check while forking Qd7. Queen promotion instead lets Black play Qc6+ and reach the illustrated mating counterattack.

startContext: Begin after ...Qc6 at 6 seconds in a complete seven-piece position. The main checking sequence, knight fork and queen-promotion mate are reconstructed from saved boards. A separate source node after ...Qb8+ demonstrates two actual stalemates; its intervening queen maneuvers are outside the encoded line.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.

sourceCorrections.claim: Automatic captions call the pawn capture Rxc4.
sourceCorrections.correction: Stable boards show the pawn on e4 and Re3 capturing it with Rxe4+. The encoded move follows the saved board, not the mistaken file name.
